content:
marta: heads-up: onboarding tessera13b-hybrid (hf export -> ONNX -> runtime). int4 path shows weird token truncation in abstractive summarization tests. not sure if it's quant artifact or tokenizer mismatch.

leo: what does "weird token truncation" look like? can you paste an example?

marta: sample input: 'In 2024 the company announced...' fp16 output: long coherent summary. int4 output: summary abruptly ends after ~40 tokens with trailing '<|endoftext|>' sometimes mid-sentence.

ci-bot: quick-run (summ-eval v1): fp16 ROUGE-1=0.48, ROUGE-L=0.39; int4 ROUGE-1=0.31, ROUGE-L=0.20; avg length fp16=96 tokens, int4=37 tokens.

vikram: short output + early eos often indicates EOS id collision or a sentinel being remapped during conversion. did the tokenizer merge step change vocab ordering?

marta: converter log shows: "merged_special_tokens: True" and we passed `--bpe-merge preserve_positions`. we otherwise used HF tokenizer files.

kyla: sometimes HF tokenizer.json has multiple synonyms for eos or placeholder tokens (e.g., both "</s>" and "<|endoftext|>") that get flattened by our tooling into a single canonical id. if our converter remaps ids, the model's learned EOS embedding index could end up pointing at a different vector post-quant.

leo: can you run a roundtrip check? encode a known phrase with HF tokenizer, then load converted tokenizer and compare id sequences. also check that highest id boundaries (vocab size) didn't shift.

marta: did that: HF encode('Hello world') -> [154, 23]. converted encode -> [154, 23]. but encode('</s>') HF -> [2], converted -> [50265]. so yes, EOS id remapped to a high index which overlaps with our truncated-pad sentinel range in runtime.

vikram: bingo. runtime treats ids >=50256 as reserved sentinels for padding/unset and clamps them. that's why outputs cut off.

aya: i tried a defensive runtime patch to treat any known eos aliases by string match instead of id threshold; re-ran 10 samples -> length restored to ~90 tokens and ROUGE-L jumped from 0.20 -> 0.36. not perfect but confirms bug. patch: https://git.internal/rw/rt/commit/eb12cd (small runtime fallback).

ci-bot: micro results with runtime patch: int4 ROUGE-L=0.36, avg length=88, latency +3%.

kyla: upstream fix is to preserve token ids during conversion or emit a tokenizer manifest containing canonical mappings. for onboarding we should assert that special token ids remain identical unless explicitly remapped with a documented mapping.

leo: also check quantizer dithering: int4 quant introduces saturation on logits for rare tokens -> if EOS id moved to an edge bucket, probability spike could prematurely select it. combine ID remap + quant saturation = amplified early stop.

marta: plan: 1) revert converter to preserve special token ids for tessera family, 2) add manifest file `tokenizer_map.json` next to model artifact listing special token strings -> ids, 3) add small CI guard that encodes a 50-sample special-token bank and diffs ids. I'll open PR 2108.

vikram: add note in model-onboard checklist: "verify special token id stability + quant saturation test". also include a short script that simulates argmax sampling after quant noise to surface early-eos spikes.

aya: i've uploaded the repro artifacts and a tiny notebook showing the argmax logit histograms: s3://redwood-temp/tessera13b/hf_vs_int4_eos_repro.ipynb

marta: thanks team. leaving the runtime fallback in for now (feature-flagged) until converter and CI are updated. tagging @kyla for the converter review. :white_check_mark:
